items.snippet: Eels vs Panthers Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 21 2026    Before You Bet
items.body_excerpt:
Eels vs Panthers Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 21 2026
July 22 nd 2026, 10:08pm , By: Scooby
The NRL is starting to heat up and with teams preparing themselves for the approaching Finals series, many of those who were previously considered out of contention are suddenly re-emerging. It makes for an exciting conclusion to the regular season, with fans enjoying exhilarating rugby league. The opening game of Round 21 is a classic derby between the Eels and Panthers in Sydney’s west. Neither wanting to lose to their opponent, the stage is set for an epic contest, regardless of where each team stands on the competition ladder.
Also, Before You Bet will be providing free previews and betting tips for EVERY game in the 2026 NRL season, so make sure to head over to our NRL Tips regularly to keep up to date with all of our free content.
Eels vs Panthers Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 21 2026
A lot to be desired
It was a week off for the Eels to lament their 28-12 road loss to the Roosters. After appearing capable of making a contest of the result after only trailing 4-nil at HT, they quickly fell away in the second half when the Roosters kicked into another gear. A lack of possession (42%) and poor completion rate (69%) hurt their cause, as did only making 7.7m per carry. Their defence was also poor, missing 40 tackles and allowing 713 PCM’s. They are a more capable team than that effort suggests but must begin to start showing it.
Defeated, again
It was an upset 14-12 home loss to the Broncos last week for the Panthers, meaning that they have won just 1 of their past 4 matches. While other factors have impacted that performance, there should be no hiding from the fact that they failed to build on a 12-8 HT lead. A lack of possession (43%) limited their attacking opportunities, as did their 78% completion rate. They were unable to use their 9.4m per carry or 5 line breaks to their advantage. They also need a shift defensively, as they missed 33 tackles and conceded 729 PCM’s. Perhaps, this is the loss they needed to have to reset them ahead of the Finals.
Stats that matter
- The Eels have won just 3 of the past 10 games between these two sides, defeated 48-20 in Round 4. Thankfully, they have a strong record at this ground compared to their opponents (61% vs 58%).
- In the past 5 games between these two sides, 2 blowout margins has seen the average margin of victory sit at 13.2 points. In the same games, the average total points is 50.4.
- It is no surprise to see the Panthers dominate on both sides of the ball this season. They score 30ppg in attack compared to the Eels 19ppg and concede only 13ppg whereas the Eels leak 29ppg.
Time to rediscover their form
Their recent run isn’t what we are accustomed to from the Panthers. There have been parts of their execution which have been positive, while others have been poor. Now, it is the time for them to get back on track with the Finals approaching. The Eels come at the right time for them to achieve this. Despite the boost which the Eels receive with Moses returning to their team, a lot more will be needed if the home team are to cause an upset. Kenny and Edwards’ absence at hooker will make it difficult again initially, but there is enough class to overcome this.
It is difficult to see any other outcome than the Panthers winning this match; therefore, the decision comes down to where the value lies in the visitors capturing victory. The average win/loss margin this season (Panthers 23.9 vs Eels 20.6) suggests that a blowout victory is ahead. The Eels will be competitive in this match to some extent; they seem to leave their best form for this matchup. That will matter little though as the Panthers regain confidence and cover the line which is lower than expected considering the talent involved with the two teams.

Gates open: 6:30pm

Tickets On Sale Now
Tickets for the Battle of the West are on sale now.
What's On
Kids can dive into Kids PARRAdise, with games, giveaways, and interactive fun, while fans of all ages can get involved in Parra Play, community activations, and grab a blue and gold flag to wave loud and proud.
Introducing our Match Day Mingle! We've partnered with dating app Thursday to bring Western Sydney singles aged 25-42 together for a night of footy and mingling. Get your tickets here
Pre-Game Fan March
For the 2026 season, fans can show their Parra Pride by joining in on our Fan March. Be part of a new game day tradition as the Blue & Gold Army marches together into the stadium. Build the hype, show your colours and arrive ready for kickoff. Everyone who joins the march will receive a free Blue & Gold flag to wave as we walk in together.
Timings: Meet outside the Parra Leagues Club multi-story car park at 6:15pm, with the March to start at 6:30pm.
Your chance to win: Enter the 50-50 Raffle
Support the Eels Foundation for your chance to win, thanks to the 50-50 Raffle. Buy your raffle tickets online now or at the game on Thursday. You don’t need to be at the game to buy tickets or win the prize.
This season, the funds raised through the 50-50 Raffle will support the Eels Foundation’s programs, including our Social Impact and Community initiatives, Academy and Pathway Programs, and facilities.
Getting To The Game
Traffic may be heavier than usual, fans are encouraged to plan ahead and consider all the available travel options.
Match tickets include free travel on public transport, simply show your match ticket to transport staff when boarding services. Visit transportnsw.info to plan your trip.
If you are driving to the game, the Justice Precinct car park (10 min walk), Parramatta Station (Wentworth Street) car park (15-20 min walk) are nearby options. Visit the City of Parramatta Parking Finder for real-time parking availability.
Get Your 2026 Eels Membership & Eels Merch
Merchandise and Membership outlets are accessible both inside and outside of CommBank Stadium, operating pre-game, during and post-game. Visit the Eels Official Store here , and view 2026 Membership options here.

For any Membership concerns, please contact membership@parraeels.com.au.

Members will be able to fast track their entry into the stadium via a dedicated Members-only entry gate at Gate B.

items.snippet: As it happened: 'Milk' man delivers as Panthers hold off Eels    NRL.com
items.body_excerpt:
Presented By
As it happened: 'Milk' man delivers as Panthers hold off Eels
The Eels were fast out of the blocks to lead 12-0 in the Battle of the West but in the end the Panthers ran them down to snare a 14th win of the season.
The Panthers came in on the back of three losses in their past four matches and were jumped early but their big guns stood up when needed despite having Thomas Jenkins and Isaiah Papali'i sin binned.
Jenkins bagged a crucial try in the 67th minute to give him 26 for the season - a new club record for the Panthers taking over from Rhys Wesser (25 in 2003).
Jenkins talks try-scoring record
The Panthers go four points clear at the top of the table and will watch on with interest as their closest chasers the Roosters and Warriors slug it out over the weekend against the Knights and Bulldogs respectively.
Follow all the action from Round 21 of the NRL Telstra Premiership on NRL.com's live blog.

Kelly kills it: In the end the Eels came up empty but not for want of trying and winger Brian Kelly typified the effort with 23 runs for 251 metres, including 98 post-contact metres. Kelly broke three tackles and also came up with a big play on half-time where he grubbered down a narrow channel on the sideline and drew a professional foul from Thomas Jenkins who was sent to the bin.
Just To'o good: Panthers winger Brian To'o was at his tackle busting best as he came up with a monster 221 metres from 21 runs while also breaking eight tackles. Paul Alamoti also came up with eight tackle breaks in a typically robust display.
Full-time: The Panthers go four points clear at the top of the table after a professional victory achieved with only 12 men on the field for a quarter of the match. The Eels led 12-0 early but couldn't come up with the big plays when the Panthers were down a man and in the end it was a 12th loss of the season for the blue and golds.
80 min: One last shot for the Eels but Billy Scott scrambles back to cover up after the Eels had chipped ahead. Game over.
Jack Williams 2nd Try
79 min: Mitch Moses puts Jack Williams into a hole between Blaize Talagi and Isaiah Papali'i and the prop has a double. Moses converts. Panthers 24-18
77 min: Brian To'o makes a safe catch off a Mitch Moses spiral bomb and bamboozles a number of Eels defenders.
74 min: Will Penisini explodes into space and the Eels look a chance to score but the final pass goes astray and Brian To'o picks up the scraps.
71 min: Tallyn Da Silva has his back turned to a Nathan Cleary clearing kick and it collects him in the back of the head. The Eels rake leaves the field for a HIA.
70 min: The Eels sweep the ball to the right and Brian Kelly puts in a grubber but Jaxen Edgar is there to cover up as he continues an impressive night in just his second NRL appearance.
Tom Jenkins' record-breaking Try
67 min: Thomas Jenkins has a club record 26 tries in a season as he finishes off a stunning team try that featured kicks by Nathan Cleary and Blaize Talagi, a great tap-back by Paul Alamoti and Eels defenders scrambling everywhere to try and shut it down. Cleary converts. Panthers 24-12
64 min: Brian To'o is worked on the ground by Will Penisini and the penalty allows the Panthers an easy out from their own end.
Papalii sent to the sin bin
61 min: The Panthers lose a player to the bin for the second time with Isaiah Papali'i marched for a professional foul as held back Mitch Moses when he was trying to support Kelma Tuilagi.
Liam Martin Try
